# Viewport and display commands

::: warning Preview version
The jsMind V2 programming API is currently a preview. The API will change in later updates. Please check this documentation anytime for the interface that is current.
:::

The display commands reachable as `jm.commands`, and the view handle they drive. Every command here changes how the map is shown and never the map itself. The zoom factor they accept is clamped to the range 0.1–4.

This page is generated from the published typings `dist/jsmind.d.ts` with TypeDoc.

## JmCommander {#JmCommander}

*Class*

Issues commands that change what is displayed, never what is stored.

### Constructor {#JmCommander.constructor}

```ts
constructor(view: JmViewHandle)
```

Creates a commander.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `view` | [JmViewHandle](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmViewHandle) | The view's capabilities. |

### centerOn {#JmCommander.centerOn}

```ts
centerOn(nodeId: string): void
```

Moves the map so that one node's centre sits in the middle of the
viewport, leaving the zoom alone.

**Throws**

- `JsMindError` When this view has not been given a map yet,
or the id is not one of that map's nodes. Closing the map does not empty
the view: centring afterwards still acts on the last map shown, instead
of throwing.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | string | Id of a node in the open mind map. |


**Returns:** The encoded image plus its dimensions.

### fitToView {#JmCommander.fitToView}

```ts
fitToView(mode?: JmFitToViewMode): void
```

Fits the map to the viewport, in the directions the caller allows.

**Remarks**

With no mode both mismatches are corrected: a map too large for the box
is shrunk until it fits, and one too small is magnified until it fills
the box - the fit a single "show me the whole map" button asks for.
`'shrink'` and `'expand'` each name one direction by taking the map's
natural size as a bound, so a caller that knows which state it is in can
correct that one and leave the other alone.

Nothing on the open path calls this. Opening a map shows it as laid out;
fitting it is a decision for whoever is showing it, made when they want
it - which is why a page either calls it after `open` or does not.

**Throws**

- `JsMindError` When this view has not been given a map yet.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` (optional) | [JmFitToViewMode](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmFitToViewMode) | `'shrink'` for a map too large for the box, `'expand'` for one too small. Omit it to correct both. |

## JmViewHandle {#JmViewHandle}

*Interface*

What the application layer is allowed to ask of the view.

### capture {#JmViewHandle.capture}

```ts
capture(options?: JmExportImageOptions): Promise<JmExportImageResult>
```

Renders the currently displayed map to an image.

**Returns:** The encoded image plus its dimensions.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `options` (optional) | [JmExportImageOptions](/en/reference/api/export#JmExportImageOptions) | Scale, format and quality. |

### centerOn {#JmViewHandle.centerOn}

```ts
centerOn(nodeId: string): void
```

Moves the map so that one node's centre sits in the middle of the
viewport.

**Remarks**

The zoom is left alone. This is a move, and a caller that centred a node
at the factor the reader had chosen should still be at that factor
afterwards - a command with "zoom to fit" in its name is a different one.

The origin is the one [JmViewHandle.panTo](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmViewHandle.panTo) would write for that
position, so it is clamped the same way: a node near the content's edge
gets as close to the middle as the band allows, and while the whole map
fits the viewport the call is a no-op because there is nowhere to move to.

A node whose ancestor is folded still has the layout position it is not
drawn at, and this centres that position. Expanding the ancestor would be
a change to the mind, which a display command does not make.

**Throws**

- `JsMindError` When this view has not been given a map yet,
or when the id is not one of that map's nodes.

A closed map is not the same as no map: nothing tells the view a map was
closed, it keeps the last one it was shown, and this centres a node of
that map instead of throwing.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nodeId` | string | Id of a node in the open mind map. |

### fitToView {#JmViewHandle.fitToView}

```ts
fitToView(mode?: JmFitToViewMode): void
```

Fits the map to the viewport, centred, in the directions the caller
allows.

**Remarks**

The zoom is chosen from the content and the box alone, so two calls on
the same map and box give the same numbers - which is what a toolbar
button pressed twice, or a gesture repeated, relies on.

With no mode both disagreements between a map and a box are corrected: a
map too large to show whole is scaled down until all of it fits, and one
smaller than its box is scaled up until it fills it. That is the
unqualified "fit" a viewer with a single button offers.

Naming a mode narrows it to one direction, for callers that already know
which state they are in and must leave the other one alone:

- `'shrink'` is for a map too large to show whole: the zoom is scaled down
until all of it fits, and never past its natural size - a map that
already fits stays at 1x rather than being blown up. This is the one to
call from a "show me everything" button or a return-from-a-corner
gesture.
- `'expand'` is for a map smaller than its box: the zoom is scaled up
until the map fills it, and never down - a map that already overflows
stays at 1x rather than being shrunk. This is the one for a page whose
canvas is the frame and wants no empty margin in it.

Every call centres the map. The two modes are bounds on the same fit -
`'shrink'` takes the natural size as a ceiling, `'expand'` as a floor -
and calling with neither takes it as no bound at all. So each call
corrects exactly what it was asked to and does nothing to the rest.

Unlike [JmViewHandle.centerOn](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmViewHandle.centerOn) this does move a map that fits: the
pan's band is empty at exactly-fitting zoom, and a fit that waited for a
clamp to move it would leave the map wherever the last gesture left it.

**Throws**

- `JsMindError` When `mode` is given as neither of the two
values, so a typo in a JavaScript caller fails loudly instead of quietly
shrinking.
- `JsMindError` When this view has not been given a map yet -
there is no content to fit. A map that was closed counts as open here:
the view keeps the last one it was shown, as it does for
[JmViewHandle.centerOn](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmViewHandle.centerOn).

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` (optional) | [JmFitToViewMode](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmFitToViewMode) | Which mismatch to correct. Omit it to correct both. |

### getViewport {#JmViewHandle.getViewport}

```ts
getViewport(): JmViewport
```

Reads the current viewport.

**Returns:** The origin, the zoom factor and the visible size.

### panBy {#JmViewHandle.panBy}

```ts
panBy(dx: number, dy: number): void
```

Moves the viewport by a distance on screen.

**Remarks**

The delta is in viewport pixels, not map pixels: a drag reports how far
the pointer travelled, and dividing by the zoom is arithmetic the view
already owns. Positive `dx` moves the map right, which shows map points
further left. Clamped the same way as [JmViewHandle.panTo](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmViewHandle.panTo), including
its no-op while the map fits the viewport.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dx` | number | Horizontal travel in viewport pixels. |
| `dy` | number | Vertical travel in viewport pixels. |

### panTo {#JmViewHandle.panTo}

```ts
panTo(x: number, y: number): void
```

Puts a map-space point at the viewport's top-left corner.

**Remarks**

`x`/`y` are the same pair [JmViewHandle.getViewport](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmViewHandle.getViewport) reports, so a
caller can read where the view is looking, keep it, and put it back. The
move is clamped to the content's bounds: the map cannot be sent into an
empty viewport it would then be unable to leave.

A clamp needs a band to clamp into, and there is one only while the map is
larger than the viewport. When the whole map fits at the current zoom the
band is empty, and this call leaves the origin unchanged: no-op, not a
move to the nearest edge and not a centring. No pan writes an origin
outside that band, which is also the answer for a `centerOn` built on top
of this one: a node can only be brought to the middle while the map
overflows the view, and while the map fits there is nothing to bring into
view.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | number | Map-space x to show at the left edge. |
| `y` | number | Map-space y to show at the top edge. |

### zoomTo {#JmViewHandle.zoomTo}

```ts
zoomTo(scale: number, anchor?: JmViewportAnchor): void
```

Changes the zoom factor, holding one point still.

**Remarks**

The anchor is explicit because a zoom has to keep something fixed, and
which something decides how the gesture feels: a wheel zooms about the
pointer, a control without a pointer position zooms about the middle of
the box. Passing the anchor in keeps the two from being mixed by accident,
and keeps the mapping from a screen point to a map point inside the view.

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scale` | number | Requested factor, clamped to the range the view accepts. |
| `anchor` (optional) | [JmViewportAnchor](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmViewportAnchor) | Point to hold still, in the view's own pixels. Defaults to the middle of the viewport. |

## JmViewport {#JmViewport}

*Interface*

A rectangle in CSS pixels, relative to the container's top-left corner.

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `canPan` | boolean | Whether a pan would move the map at this zoom. |
| `height` | number | Visible height in CSS pixels. |
| `scale` | number | Current zoom factor, 1 being unscaled. |
| `width` | number | Visible width in CSS pixels. |
| `x` | number | Map-space x shown at the viewport's left edge. |
| `y` | number | Map-space y shown at the viewport's top edge. See [JmViewport.x](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmViewport.x). |

## JmViewportAnchor {#JmViewportAnchor}

*Interface*

A point in the view's own box, measured from its top-left corner.

**Remarks**

This is not a map coordinate and not a page coordinate: it is what a pointer
event carries once the box's own origin has been subtracted, which is the one
thing a caller holding a pointer has to work out. Turning it into a map
position is the view's job, and [JmViewHandle.zoomTo](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmViewHandle.zoomTo) is the only place
it crosses back in.

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | number |  |
| `y` | number |  |

## JmFitToViewMode {#JmFitToViewMode}

*Type*

Which mismatch between the map and its box a fit corrects.

**Remarks**

A map and a box can disagree in two ways, and they want different answers: a
map too large to show whole has to be scaled down, and a map smaller than the
box may be scaled up to fill it - or left at its natural size, which is what
a viewer showing text wants. [JmViewHandle.fitToView](/en/reference/api/viewport#JmViewHandle.fitToView) takes one of these
and does that one thing, never the other; leaving it out corrects both.
